child: Ask {member} to join you for {activity}.
adult: Invite {member} to join you for {activity} this week.

child: Ask {member} to teach you about {theirActivity}, or do it together.
adult: Join {member} in {theirActivity} – let them lead and teach you.

child: Have 15 minutes of special time with {member} – you choose what to do, no phones!
adult: Give {member} 15 minutes of special time: they choose, you follow, no phones.

child: Go for a walk with {member} and spot 5 interesting things.
adult: Go for a walk with {member}. Let the conversation wander wherever it goes.

child: Cook or bake something with {member}.
adult: Cook a meal together with {member} – one of you picks the recipe, the other is the helper.

child: Look through old photos with {member}. Find the funniest one!
adult: Look through old photographs with {member} and share the stories behind them.

child: Plan a family breakfast – you choose the menu!
adult: Plan a slow family breakfast this weekend. Everyone gets to choose one thing on the table.

child: Add 2 songs to a family playlist and ask everyone else to add theirs.
adult: Start a family playlist – everyone adds two songs and explains one of them.

child: Watch a movie with the family – all phones in a basket!
adult: Family movie night with all phones in a basket. Talk about the movie afterwards.

child: Call or visit {extended} and ask them about when they were your age.
adult: Phone or visit {extended}. Ask them a question you've never asked before.

child: Help plan a braai and invite {friend}!
adult: Plan a braai or get-together and invite {friend}.

child: Plan a date with {member} – you choose where to go!
adult: Plan a date night (or date afternoon) with {member}. Put it in the calendar today.

child: Plan the family week together on a big piece of paper.
adult: Sit down together and plan the week – include one thing each person is looking forward to.

child: Help {member} with one of their jobs today, without being asked.
adult: Notice something {member} usually does alone, and do it with them today.

child: Have dinner with {member} and ask: 'What was the best and worst part of your day?'
adult: At dinner, everyone shares a high and a low from their day. No fixing – just listening.

child: Go and watch {member} do something they love – a game, a practice, a hobby.
adult: Show up for something {member} cares about – a match, a performance or a hobby – and just watch.

child: Grow something with {member}: plant a seed and look after it together.
adult: Start something that grows with {member} – a herb pot, a vegetable patch, a sourdough starter.

child: Make a family 'bucket list' of 10 things you want to do together this year.
adult: Write a family bucket list together. Pick one thing to do this month.

child: Have a 'yes afternoon' with {member} – they can pick (almost) anything to do!
adult: Give {member} a 'yes hour': you say yes to their (reasonable) ideas for the whole hour.

child: Visit {extended} and bring them something you made.
adult: Plan a visit to {extended}. Bring something homemade or a photo to talk about.

child: Invite {friend} over for a braai and help plan the food.
adult: Host {friend} for a braai or potjie. Let everyone in the family choose one thing on the menu.

child: Make a family tree with {member}. Ask about the people you don't know.
adult: Make a family tree with {member} and share stories about the people on it.

child: Go stargazing or watch the sunset with {member}.
adult: Watch a sunset or stargaze with {member}. Leave the phones inside.

child: Do a 'tech-free evening' with the whole family: games, stories, music.
adult: Plan a whole tech-free evening as a family. Agree together what you'll do instead.

child: Make breakfast in bed for {member}.
adult: Surprise {member} with breakfast or coffee in bed.
